findings.message: Canvas and study layout pass. The PNG is 1024x1536 and contains exactly six separated studies in two columns by three rows: three-quarter head, front head, anatomical left profile, rear head, full-body front, and full-body three-quarter working posture. Crowns, chins, hands, and feet are visible, with no borders, labels, story text, props, environment, or other characters.

Core identity and production cues substantially pass. Close black curls, early temple silver, thin rectangular glasses, long slim adult proportions, reserved expression, chore jacket, dark trousers, work shoes, and the glove-handling pose are coherent across the sheet and recognizable from the approved Daniel identity input.

The required narrow healed scar across Daniel's nose bridge is not clearly visible and stable across the three-quarter, front, and profile head studies. The brief makes the scar a signature continuity feature and explicitly requires it in the review check.

The finish uses broad continuous gray modeling on the face, neck, and clothing plus soft feathered fades beneath the bust studies. The locked finish requires skin to remain mostly white paper with discrete screentone, sparse functional hatching, and flat blacks, and excludes smooth gradient, airbrush, painterly grayscale, and vignette-like fading.

Generation lineage and filename need normalization. No structured job or exact executed prompt was supplied, and the download is named daniel-tomas.png although the raster contains Daniel only. Review is therefore against the approved identity input and Daniel brief; a corrected candidate should use a new versioned Daniel-only filename.
No image was edited, regenerated, converted, renamed, or promoted. The Downloads original remains unchanged and a byte-identical copy is retained only as internal review evidence.
